comparator.sourceNotes: The visually inspected2026–2027 TER Annex1 page20 is the controlling current framework, with60EC in each year. Its curriculum chart is a raster image and is absent from extracted text; Annex2 old-degree tables must not supply its credits. The selected30EC choice pathway is a15EC approved minor plus three5EC electives; Annex4 page29 places the last elective in block3.3 alongside Advanced Research Skills. Articles3.5–3.6,4.1 and8.1 govern approval/progression. The stakeholder track has two5EC courses and one7EC bachelor project, counted once although it spans two blocks. This current framework is not a guarantee of unchanged later-year delivery for a2026 entrant.

components.name: Minor
components.note: One permitted 15-EC minor from the approved EUR or authorised LDE offer; the choice needs to meet programme rules. Year 1 must be completed before entry.

components.name: Elective space 1
components.note: A 5-EC elective within the 30-EC choice space. External units require Examination Board approval for level, supervision, limited overlap and fit with programme outcomes.

components.name: Elective space 2
components.note: A second 5-EC elective within the same regulated choice space; elective status does not guarantee unrestricted choice or a place.

components.name: Elective space 3
components.note: The final 5-EC elective in this minor-plus-electives pathway occurs in block 3.3 alongside Advanced Research Skills, as shown in the formal curriculum.

components.name: International Business and External Stakeholder Management
components.note: Selected track course. A full track must be taken; courses cannot be mixed across tracks. Allocation depends on preferences and capacity, so first choice is not guaranteed.

components.name: BSc Project Navigating Stakeholders in Global Business
components.note: A single 7-EC bachelor project belonging to the complete selected track; it spans blocks 3.4 and 3.5 and combines individual and group work. Year 1 must be complete before entry.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces much of the general economics, law, communication and leadership mix with programming, mathematics, algorithms, databases, machine learning, deep learning and AI ethics.

alternatives.concept: Financial markets and quantitative business decisions, combining accounting, investment appraisal, securities, banking and economic behaviour with econometrics, numerical methods, statistical inference and optimisation. International business, strategy, public economics and moral reasoning situate financial and managerial decisions in their institutional and social setting.

alternatives.labelRationale: The actual curriculum links financial markets, securities, banking, accounting and investment appraisal with economics, business strategy and mathematical and computational decision methods. The label does not promise an international accounting or corporate-tax specialisation.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The academic priorities shift from broad managerial functions and leadership to financial institutions, economic explanation and rigorous quantitative decisions. Economic and financial institutions, accounting, behaviour and public policy distinguish this programme from the neural-network, database and consumer-technology emphasis of the AI route. International accounting and multinational-tax equivalence are not asserted.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three evidence-backed responses survive. Current BENBUSI112 and BENBUSI312 evidence overturns the earlier finance rejection: management accounting, discounted cash flow, securities, banking, regulation and risk combine with economic explanation and rigorous decision analytics into a coherent related route. It does not reproduce international accounting, multinational tax or the complete RSM capital-strategies track. Responsible business remains concretely represented through stakeholder governance, public policy and ethical reasoning. Every pair passes qualitative and 30-EC distinctness.

notes.text: RSM provides a compulsory sequence across business functions, a complete third-year track and a required bachelor project. UCR offers broad business and management, business with technical AI, and financial markets with quantitative business decisions. Introductory accounting, management-accounting and investment-appraisal work and securities/banking study are present, but these options do not reproduce RSM’s full operations, supply-chain, human-resource, international accounting/tax or particular track/project sequence. Shared rows show specific partial relationships rather than course equivalence.

audience.programmeDescription: International Business Administration at Rotterdam School of Management, Erasmus University Rotterdam is a three-year, English-taught BSc. Students study the major business functions in an international setting, develop quantitative research skills, use regulated choice space and complete one third-year track with a bachelor project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options pursue broad international business and management, business with technical AI, or financial markets and quantitative business decisions. Each has a substantial business basis with different methods and priorities. They do not reproduce RSM’s complete functional sequence, multinational accounting and tax specialisms, or required track/project structure. Shared rows indicate specific partial relationships; blank cells preserve gaps.
